city_policy: A business is listed only when its own website states the service. The page links that source. If a price or a turnaround time is not on the site, the listing says so instead of guessing.
This is not a complete list of every studio, pharmacy, or big-box photo counter in the area. National mail-in labs are on the comparison page, not repeated under each city.
city_checklist: Count the tapes, reels, and photos, and note the formats. VHS-C, Hi8, MiniDV, and Super 8 are not the same job as a standard VHS cassette.
Ask what happens if a tape is moldy, squealing, or snapped. Do not play a tape that looks moldy or that screams when it starts.
Ask whether you receive a file you can copy (usually MP4) or only a DVD. A DVD is a convenient extra, and a poor only copy.
Ask the current turnaround and whether the originals come back with the job. Get that in writing if the box is leaving your house.
Commercial movies and recorded television are copyrighted. A legitimate lab will refuse them.
